what: Answer to the checker's Nov 10 item: explain each of the nudge's four positive-residual cycles in E0031 (the checker called them energy-gain cycles; the collision gain counter is zero in all four). Each run was replayed from its seed with the nudge engine (b608fef) exactly as referee/long_contact.py runs it (32 stops per cycle, re-sort after every cycle), and the per-cycle audit residual recomputed together with the potential energy the nudge adds by lifting spheres (EN_NUDGE, not booked by the audit).
findings: All four replays reproduce the audit residual bit for bit (1.237e-08, 1.637e-08, 4.032e-08, 5.797e-08 of throughput).
The nudge's own lift accounts for 1.0e-13 to 3.1e-13 of throughput in these cycles: it does not explain them.
No collision in any of the four cycles gains energy in its dissipation frame (energy_gains 0).

In cycle 574 of nudge-g5-f0.5-d5-s2, 99.9% of the residual builds up in the first 7 of 1024 windows of the cycle (phases 0 to 0.0068), which hold 32055 to 113117 events each, and grows smoothly with the event count rather than in one event.

Over the E0031 2D nudge cycles audited by 23:30 on Nov 11 (22406), audit failures occur only in cycles with more than 300 events per particle; 4 of 134 failures are positive, all in cycles above 1000 events per particle; the log of |residual| correlates with the log of events per particle (0.46).

Reading: the four cycles are the positive tail of an accounting drift that accumulates over hundreds of thousands of near-contact plate and pair events just after phase 0, when the plate moves fastest and per-event lab-frame energies are large compared with their changes. The exact per-event mechanism (which rounding) is not identified; it is not the nudge's lift and not a collision that gains energy.
mechanism_identified: Event-by-event over the first 1/1024 of cycle 574 (113117 events): the residual (2.105e-06 in energy units) is carried by pair collisions (2.104e-06; plate 1.1e-09). Repeating the same window with the engine's energy accumulators set to zero at its start (bookkeeping only; identical event counts) gives a residual of 1.43e-11. Before the window the pair-dissipation accumulator held 1.63e+06, where one unit in the last place is about 2.3e-10, so each small per-collision energy change added to it is rounded by up to that much. The four positive-residual cycles are therefore round-off in the engine's running energy totals, which grow with run length, during cycles with many collisions. They are not energy put in by the nudge. The same effect should affect any engine's audit late in long chatter-heavy runs, with either sign.
